_comment: Authoritative CORE/ADAPTER/ADAPTER_FRONTMATTER/COUPLED classification, token classes and per-path vendor-coupling allowances, enforced by scripts/check-vendor-coupling.sh. THIS JSON is the single source of truth the gate reads; the gate hard-codes no token, no glob and no allowance, so every policy change is a reviewable diff here. RATCHET SEMANTICS: breach = actual > allowance; actual < allowance PASSES (debt paid down is never a CI failure). To add a reference to a ratcheted path, raise its allowance in the SAME PR AND add or change its one-line entry in `allowance_reasons` (the gate's raise_check compares with the base manifest and refuses a new or raised allowance whose reason is missing or INHERITED unchanged from the base), which puts the raise and its argument in front of a reviewer (counting LESS needs a reason too: an exemption of a path that held an allowance, a token removed from token_classes, or a raised frontmatter bound each needs an added or changed `policy_reasons` entry) — the same convention prompt-token-budgets.json uses for prompt budgets. COUNTING (schema 2): the gate counts LITERAL fixed-string occurrences of every token in `token_classes` per tracked file (git ls-files, then a POSIX-awk pass), counting every occurrence rather than every matching line — a line-based count would let a second reference hide on an existing line — and reports a total per token class plus a flat total. Overlapping tokens are resolved by `token_overlap_rule` (leftmost-longest: each occurrence is counted ONCE, for the class of the longest token matching at that position). Agent and command files are ADAPTER_FRONTMATTER: their leading YAML frontmatter is the harness's own header and is not counted, their bodies are. HONEST LIMIT: a reference ASSEMBLED AT RUNTIME (built by concatenation or indirection) contains no literal token and is invisible to this mechanism; a green run means 'no new LITERAL coupling', not 'no new coupling'. A coupling mechanism with no declared token is invisible too, until a class names it. SCOPE LIMIT: only `scan_roots` is scanned. Root prose (README.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md), the sibling plugins (stackpack/, mysql-mcp/) and .github/ are deliberately UNSCANNED, not certified clean — release prose names the harness by necessity and would force an allowance bump every release, which is how a gate earns being switched off. REFUTED ASSUMPTION, recorded on purpose: the source requirement assumed these references 'are dominated by legitimately-adapter surfaces (commands/hooks/agent frontmatter)'. Measured on the base commit of this change, adapter-ish surfaces were 131/278 = 47% and core-ish surfaces 139/278 = 50% — the assumption is REFUTED; adapter surfaces are NOT dominant. The mitigating fact is that the CORE allowance table is nonetheless small, so ratcheting it down later is tractable. (Those 278/131/139 figures are MATCHING-LINE counts from the requirement's own measurement, kept verbatim as the historical record; this gate counts OCCURRENCES, which are >= line counts, so the numbers below are legitimately larger.) The allowance values below were produced by `bash scripts/check-vendor-coupling.sh --print-allowances` and committed as measured — never hand-typed.
token_overlap_rule_note: How one occurrence is attributed when tokens overlap. `leftmost-longest` is the only rule the gate implements: a line is scanned left to right; at the leftmost position where any token matches, the LONGEST token matching there is counted once, for its own class, and the scan resumes after it. So no byte is counted twice, and a long token that contains a shorter one (the runtime_identity session-id variable contains the install_root env-var prefix) counts once, for the long token's class. The rule is implemented in awk rather than left to `grep -oF`, whose choice among overlapping `-e` patterns is unspecified (BSD and GNU need not agree). A token declared twice is an ERROR. Like count_mode, an unknown value is rejected rather than ignored.

install_root.note: The original four tokens (schema 1's flat list): the plugin-install-root variable, the harness env-var prefix, the headless CLI invocation, and the harness config directory. Paths and invocations a non-Claude harness does not have.

orchestration.note: The host's subagent spawn / poll / message vocabulary. Another harness has its own (or none), so every reference in a counted body is a porting cost.

hook_protocol.note: Host hook event names and hook payload / response fields.

runtime_identity.note: Environment variables the host sets to identify the running process or session. The session-id variable BEGINS WITH the install_root env-var prefix token; one occurrence of it is ONE reference, counted under runtime_identity only, by the leftmost-longest `token_overlap_rule` (pinned by a test in scripts/test-check-vendor-coupling.sh, which runs on GNU CI).

sdk_binding.note: The host vendor's npm package scope. The SDK spike loads its SDK through a variable holding the module name (a dynamic import a static import scan would miss); the literal match still sees it because that constant spells the scope in one string, as do the spike's package manifests. A module name built by concatenation would be invisible — the runtime-assembly limit stated in the _comment.

model_names.note: Claude model aliases in CODE/CONFIG shape only: a `model:` key followed by one of the three aliases, and each alias as a double-quoted string. Chosen by measurement on this change's base commit over the surfaces the gate COUNTS after this change (agent/command bodies with frontmatter stripped, skills, docs, scripts, the SDK spike): every hit of every chosen string was a true model-alias reference (spawn-time model parameters, JSON and fixture model fields, citations of a config value) and none was a prose false positive. The quoted third alias was not in the requirement's candidate list; it was added because it measured the same way (true references only) and leaving it out would be an arbitrary hole beside the other two. REJECTED: the bare alias words, which also match table cells and prose that names a model, so counting them would inflate allowances with noise. NOT COUNTED, a known gap: full versioned model IDs (vendor prefix, family, version), which were outside the candidate set. Most `model:` keys live in agent frontmatter, which is adapter surface and excluded. Per-candidate counts are in the PR that introduced this class, not restated here.

unclassified_default_note: A path matched by no class glob is treated as CORE with an allowance of 0, so a brand-new directory cannot silently become a coupling haven: the first vendor reference added to it fails CI until someone classifies it here. The gate rejects `adapter` as a default outright — a blanket adapter default would exempt the entire tree and make the ratchet vacuous.
glob_syntax_note: Globs are shell `case` patterns evaluated against the repo-relative path, where `*` DOES match `/`. So `loomwright/skills/*` covers the whole subtree, and no `**` form is needed. ADAPTER is matched first, then COUPLED, then CORE — which is what lets a single-file adapter exemption win over the broader CORE glob that contains it.

adapter.note: Adapter surfaces may name any harness freely and are NOT counted at all. loomwright/hooks is the hook manifest and its prompt surfaces — hooks.json IS the Claude adapter, and demanding neutrality from it would be demanding it stop working. Agents and commands USED to be listed here as whole files; they are adapter_frontmatter now (only their frontmatter is exempt), because their bodies are the prose a non-Claude harness would have to run. The two .claude-plugin MANIFESTS (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json and loomwright/.claude-plugin/plugin.json) are literally the vendor's packaging format, and are named individually rather than by a directory glob ON PURPOSE: a `.claude-plugin/*` glob also swept in .claude-plugin/README.md, which is prose rather than a manifest, silently exempting its references while this note claimed to be exempting only manifests. That prose file is now COUPLED and ratcheted like any other doc. loomwright/scripts/resolve-loomwright-root.sh is exempt DELIBERATELY and load-bearingly: its entire job is to name the harness variable ONCE so that nothing else has to, and a gate that flagged it would be flagging the seam that exists to remove the coupling everywhere else.

adapter_frontmatter.note: Counted EXCEPT for a leading YAML frontmatter block. Agent and command files open with a frontmatter header the harness itself parses (name, tools, model, hooks) — that block is the adapter surface and is not counted. Everything after it is the agent's or command's actual instructions, which a non-Claude harness would have to run, so it is ratcheted like CORE and may hold an allowance (unlike a whole-file ADAPTER path, where an allowance is an ERROR). Frontmatter = a `---` on LINE 1 up to the first later line that is exactly `---`; a file whose line 1 is not `---` is counted whole; a frontmatter that never closes is counted whole (an unterminated block must not hide a file); a `---` rule later in the body is body. Matched after ADAPTER and before COUPLED/CORE. Only `*.md` is listed: a non-markdown file added under these directories falls to unclassified_default and is counted whole. BOUNDED: `max_frontmatter_lines` caps the lines between the two delimiters, set comfortably above the longest real agent or command frontmatter measured when it was introduced; a longer block is not frontmatter for the gate and the whole file is counted, because a YAML block scalar (a key followed by an indented text block) could otherwise carry a whole body inside the header. Within the bound that residue remains, which is why RAISING the bound needs a `policy_reasons` entry (id `bound:max_frontmatter_lines`).

coupled.note: Grandfathered debt. loomwright/skills and loomwright/docs carry real, already-paid-for coupling: skills document harness-specific workflows and docs describe the harness by name. They are ratcheted exactly like CORE — the allowance simply starts from a higher measured baseline. Classifying them COUPLED rather than ADAPTER is the point: an adapter exemption would never be paid down, whereas a COUPLED allowance can only fall. .claude-plugin/README.md is listed explicitly for the reason given in the adapter note: it is prose that sits in a manifest directory, so it is classified by what it IS, not by where it lives.

core.note: The portable core: the plugin's runtime scripts (shell and python under loomwright/scripts, plus the TypeScript SDK spike). These are the files a non-Claude adapter would have to run unmodified, so every literal harness reference in them is a porting cost. A file under these globs that carries references holds an entry in `allowances`; every other file's allowance is 0, which is precisely what makes a NEW reference in a currently-clean script fail. COUNT BASIS: the gate counts every token of every class in `token_classes`, so how many core files hold an entry is DERIVED from the `allowances` table (its keys under these globs) and deliberately not restated here — a number written in this note is a second copy that drifts, and a single-token grep measures a different, smaller basis. The root `scripts/` directory (this repo's own CI gates) is not listed here — it falls through to `unclassified_default`, which is also core, so it is ratcheted identically without needing a glob. loomwright/sdk-spike/* is listed EXPLICITLY even though it would already reach the same verdict via unclassified_default. The behaviour is identical; the message is not. Without the glob, the first person to add a reference there is told only that an unclassified path breached a default they have to go read about — a poor answer to 'why did CI fail?'. It is ratcheted rather than ADAPTER-exempt on purpose: the spike is an experimental SDK runner and therefore looks like an adapter, but its measured coupling is narrow — the SDK package binding (the `sdk_binding` class) in its package.json, its lockfile and the runner's package-scope string, plus its README's prose — and each of those paths holds a measured, reasoned allowance (see `allowances` and `allowance_reasons`). An exemption would grant a licence it has not earned and would silently absorb any future coupling of every other class; ratcheted, any new reference there is a reviewable, reasoned allowance raise like anywhere else.

allowances_note: Per-path measured baselines. A value is the count the gate itself measured on the commit that introduced or last raised it — never a hand-typed number. An entry for a path that does not exist, or for an ADAPTER-classified path, is an ERROR (the manifest stays self-cleaning, and an allowance cannot be used to quietly reclassify a file). A path absent from this map has an allowance of 0. TWO ENTRIES ARE NEW COUPLING INTRODUCED BY THE CHANGE THAT CREATED THIS FILE, and are called out rather than buried in the table: (1) `loomwright/docs/vendor-coupling-manifest.json` = 4, which is this file's own `vendor_tokens` declaration — the manifest is NOT exempted from its own scan, so adding a fifth token requires bumping this number in the same edit, which is the intended visibility rather than an inconvenience; (2) `loomwright/scripts/test-resolve-loomwright-root.sh` = 10, the resolver's self-test, which must name the harness variable literally in order to test the harness arm at all. It is deliberately CORE-with-an-allowance rather than ADAPTER: the resolver's exemption is justified by it being the single seam, and that argument does not extend to its test. Obfuscating those references so the counter could not see them would have been the dishonest alternative — it would lower the number without lowering the coupling. SELF-RAISE, recorded on purpose: this file's own allowance moved 4 -> 5 in the same edit that added a COUNT-BASIS WARNING to classes.core.note, because that warning names a vendor token literally in order to warn about it. That is the raise rule working as intended, not a loophole -- the manifest is scanned like anything else, so the cost of explaining the mechanism in prose is a visible, reviewable +1 rather than a silent exemption. It also answers the obvious question: there is NO deadlock. Adding a token raises this file's count by one and the allowance is bumped in the same edit, exactly as any other path would be. Both changes only make EXISTING references visible — the re-baseline itself added no reference anywhere — so every raised or new entry is a measurement, and each carries an `allowance_reasons` entry naming what moved it. This file's own entry rose because it now declares every token of every class literally (the manifest is scanned like anything else) and because the class notes describe the mechanisms; the notes DESCRIBE tokens rather than quote them wherever that stays legible. Later edits of these notes within the same change moved that one entry again (the first review iteration removed a self-reference from a class note, so it fell; the ratchet-hardening pass after it re-measured it), always by --print-allowances and never by a new reference elsewhere. From this change on, a raise without an added or changed reason fails CI.
allowance_reasons_note: One-line reason per path, REQUIRED for every allowance that is new or higher than the base manifest's (base = $VENDOR_COUPLING_BASE, else origin/main; read with `git show <base>:<this file's repo-relative path>`). The reason must be ADDED or CHANGED versus the base: an inherited, unchanged reason does not justify a new raise, so a reason written for one raise never pre-authorises the next. A key with no matching `allowances` entry, or a value that is not a non-empty one-line string, is an ERROR — this map is self-cleaning like the allowance table. When the base is unresolvable the gate prints `raise_check: skipped (no base)`; CI fetches the base and sets VENDOR_COUPLING_REQUIRE_BASE=1 so it never skips there. The entries introduced by the schema-2 re-baseline (agnostic-phase1/01) say which newly counted token classes or which newly counted body moved the path; the re-baseline added no reference anywhere, it only made existing ones visible (this manifest's own entry was re-measured after later note edits in the same change). Reasons are compared NORMALISED (trimmed, internal whitespace collapsed to one space), so a whitespace-only edit of an inherited reason is still inherited and certifies nothing.

policy_reasons_note: One-line reasons for policy changes that make the gate count LESS, keyed by a namespaced id, REQUIRED (added or changed versus the base manifest, compared normalised exactly like allowance_reasons) whenever the change is made: `exempt:<path>` when a path that held a base allowance above zero still exists but is now ADAPTER, newly ADAPTER_FRONTMATTER, or outside the scanned set; `token:<token>` when a token the base declared (in token_classes or the retired flat list) is declared by no class any more; `bound:max_frontmatter_lines` when the frontmatter bound is raised. Without this map those moves would absorb coupling growth with no reason at all, because the allowance table never sees them. An entry certifies nothing once the base carries it unchanged, so a stale one is harmless and may be pruned; an unknown namespace or a malformed value is an ERROR.
